今天早报聚焦中东地区紧张局势加剧及美国政府停摆的最新动态。

  • 沙特、阿联酋或加入伊朗战争

    据《华尔街日报》报道，沙特和阿联酋正考虑加入与伊朗的冲突。沙特同意向美国军方开放法赫德空军基地，这被视为对伊朗敌人的支持。此外，阿联酋关闭了一家由伊朗经营的医院和俱乐部。

    这一消息加剧了中东地区的紧张局势，并可能引发更大规模的军事行动。

  • 美国参议员接近达成国土安全部停摆协议

    共和党参议员与总统特朗普在白宫会面后，参议员凯蒂·布里特表示她认为已找到解决五周来部分国土安全部关门僵局的方案。民主党领袖查克·舒默也在讨论中。

    如果达成协议，这将有助于缓解美国航空旅行中的混乱状况。

  • Saudi, UAE Could Reportedly Join Iran War; Senate Inches Toward DHS Deal

    Today's top stories, with context, in just 15 minutes. On today's podcast: 1) Fighting between Iran and the US-Israeli alliance continued unabated, even as President Trump claimed talks are under way to end the conflict. Iran launched overnight missile and drone attacks on the Israeli cities of Eilat, Dimona and Tel Aviv, as well as US bases in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a drone in its eastern region, and Kuwait said some power lines were put out of service after an Iranian attack. Sirens sounded in Bahrain. In Iran, the Fars news agency reported US-Israeli attacks that damaged a gas pressure-regulation plant and an administrative building in the central city of Isfahan. There was also a strike on a pipeline supplying gas to the Khorramshahr Combined Cycle Power Plant in southwestern Iran, according to Fars. The attacks continued after Trump postponed strikes on Iran&rsquo;s energy infrastructure, citing &ldquo;productive conversations&rdquo; with Tehran. The US president&rsquo;s claims of behind-the-scenes diplomacy were widely denied by Iranian officials, causing confusion over the participants in the talks and the parameters of a potential deal. 2) Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have taken steps toward joining the Iran war, the Wall Street Journal reported, potentially signaling an escalation of the fighting. Saudi Arabia agreed to give the US military access to King Fahd Air Base, the WSJ reported, citing people familiar with the matter, an apparent reversal after saying its bases couldn&rsquo;t be used to attack its longtime rival. The newspaper also cited people familiar as saying the United Arab Emirates closed an Iranian-owned hospital and club &mdash; undercutting a key source of support for Tehran. 3) Senators in both parties expressed rising optimism late Monday about reaching an agreement to end the five-week partial shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security, which has increasingly snarled air travel across the United States. After Republican senators met at the White House with President Trump on Monday, Senator Katie Britt of Alabama, a key negotiator, said she thought they had a solution to the impasse. On the floor she could be seen talking with members of both parties including Chuck Schumer, the Democrat leader. Schumer said &ldquo;both sides are working in a serious way&rdquo; as he left the Capitol after a day that began when Trump soured the talks with demands that Republicans tie passage of the partisan SAVE America Act voting legislation to Homeland Security funding. 本期节目聚焦于NCAA锦标赛的独家转播权。

  • 大卫·莱维：为什么你能观看所有NCAA锦标赛的比赛

    大卫·莱维在《The Deal》节目中讲述了他如何促成特纳广播公司与CBS达成协议，使得每一场NCAA锦标赛比赛都能在全国电视上播出。

    这是NCAA锦标赛历史上的一次突破性事件。

  • David Levy is the Reason You’re Watching March Madness

    It&rsquo;s brackets season! And you can watch all 67 games of both the women&rsquo;s and men&rsquo;s NCAA tournament on national TV, thanks to David Levy. Levy spent 33 years at Turner Broadcasting, eventually serving as its president, where he expanded the network&rsquo;s NBA coverage. Levy is probably best known for brokering a $10.8 billion rights agreement that made every March Madness game available nationally across CBS and the Turner networks for the very first time. In this episode of The Deal, Alex and Jason talk to Levy about the ins and outs of the March Madness deal. He also tells the story of how he got Shaq to fill Inside the NBA&rsquo;s fourth chair and why the key to that show&rsquo;s success is letting Charles Barkley talk. Finally, Levy shares more about his current venture, Horizon Sports & Experiences, and why he&rsquo;s betting big on women&rsquo;s sports and pickleball. 聚焦全球能源依赖和清洁能源的未来。

  • 油价上涨重燃电动车兴趣

    在伊朗战争的影响下，石油价格上涨引发了消费者对电动汽车和其他清洁能源技术的兴趣。Bloomberg记者Todd Woody和Zero播客主持人Akshat Rathi与Sarah Holder讨论了高油价重新点燃的迹象，并探讨了企业及国家如何应对这一情况。

    这反映了全球能源依赖的变化以及对清洁能源未来的关注。

  • $100 to Fill Up Your Tank? Some Drivers Say No Thanks

    As the war with Iran drags out and oil prices remain turbulent, it raises the question of whether &mdash; and how &mdash; prolonged conflict in the Middle East might impact global fossil fuel dependence and the future of renewable energy. On today&rsquo;s Big Take podcast, Bloomberg reporter Todd Woody and Zero podcast host Akshat Rathi join Sarah Holder to discuss early signs that the high cost of oil is reigniting consumer interest in electronic vehicles and other clean energy technologies, and how companies and countries are beginning to respond.
